Text:
A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Isekai stories and language barriers
I was wondering how you all are feeling about language barriers when it comes to isekai stories. Do you like them? Dislike them? Or are you neutral about it? I'm currently planning an isekai story, and I just can't make up my mind if the protagonist should just magically understand everyone, or if there should be a language barrier. On one hand, I think a language barrier would be more realistic and would make things even more interesting. It would add a whole new sub-plot and even layers to already planned out plots. On the other hand, it would make things *so much more complicated*, and as someone who has learned several languages I know how awfully long it takes to get fluent in a language. Yes, I could speed it up, because it's fiction but I just know I couldn't bring myself to. I would constantly think "Yeah, no way you've learned that so fast". 🫠 I also worry that it would get boring after a while, if the language struggle drags on too long (not only for the reader, but for me as well). An alterantive would be to solve it with magic. Having her learn the language for a while, but then either giving her the ability to speak the language fluently, or at least learn it faster, before the communication problem overstays its welcome. That would make sense within the world’s logic, but it also feels a little cheap. I know this is ultimately my decision, but I was hoping to hear some opinions (and maybe idea, if you want to share) to help me make up my mind. Because right now, that's the only thing that stops from from starting the story and it's starting to drive me insane. 😭



They receive the following reply to their post:

Omg, totally get it! Languages are like, so tricky. Maybe magic is like a solid cheat code, right? But yeah, it's your story, so you do you! Can't wait to see what you pick! 😊

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

A good site to publish a novel chapter by chapter?
I have a novel and I would like to publish it online in small portions, and possibly gain some attention, perhaps even a small group of followers. Are there any good sites for this out there? I don't want to simply start a solitary blog and try to draw attention to it, so I guess I'm looking for a site with some kind of community. (Genre: SF/Fantasy/Drama)



They receive the following reply to their post:

I have to disagree with anyone who says Wattpad isn’t a good option. Yeah, it’s a crowded platform and it has a lot of fanfics and teen romance stories, but there are also some pretty awesome gems in sci-fi and fantasy! Plus, there’s an actual community there—people who will give feedback and encouragement. And there’s Royal Road. It’s mostly aimed at teen dudes, but if your project appeals to them, it’s sometimes possible to build a big audience quickly. They favor ongoing work with quick chapter production, but you don’t necessarily have to rely on reader feedback, so it’s a bit more secure for untested work. And I know that writing is sometimes seen as a lonely endeavor, but I’ve found communities on these platforms where people hype each other up and offer real support. There are folks that end up meeting in person, it's true. No matter what platform you choose, I think it's worth exploring a few different options to see what fits your style best, y’know? There’s always Scribophile or Reddit itself if you want to start a blog. So many choices, I don’t know what to pick either!

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Sci fj western short story. Feedback would be appreciated
Some feedback for my Sci Fi Western short story would be appreciated. Hello all, I’m crafting a sci fi western story and world and I’ve started writing short stories to get a feel for the overall story. The link below is the first half (second draft) a short story I am writing. [Short Story](https://docs.google.com/file/d/1GkEe0B_bw2CHowsDbHefgtyLrXOcAuGe/edit?usp=docslist_api&filetype=msword) It’s just over 2000 words so far. They receive the following reply to their post:

Hey, sci-fi westerns? Sounds like cowboys in space! I mean, who wouldn't want a laser gun showdown? I glanced at it, but I'm not sure if the tumbleweed rolls the same way in space. Good luck with that third-person thing, though. Sounds fancy! What's next, a talking horse with a jetpack? Can't wait to see how it finishes! Keep at it!

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Validation: 100% Grass Fed Beef Tallow Sunscreen to Protect Our Oceans Reefs
Hey friends! 🌊🐠 I’m working on a new idea: a **grass-fed beef tallow** product designed to **help protect our ocean’s reefs**. Unlike many products labeled as “reef-safe,” which still contain harmful chemicals, this would be **100% natural and eco-friendly**—perfect for people who love the water as much as I do. Here’s the truth: **some major sunscreen brands claiming to be reef-safe still include chemicals like oxybenzone and octinoxate**, which are harmful to coral reefs. This product would be a simple, natural alternative to keep reefs safe while giving back to conservation efforts. The plan is to sell it for **$49.99**, with a portion of the proceeds directly supporting **ocean conservation**. What do you think? Would you give it a try? Let me know in the comments or DM me—I’d love your feedback!



They receive the following reply to their post:

Sounds like an awesome idea! I totally dig the concept of using natural ingredients like beef tallow for sunscreen, especially if it's supporting ocean conservation. I'm all for anything that takes steps to protect coral reefs – they're so essential to our oceans, and it's terrifying how much damage has been done already. Plus, knowing exactly what you're putting on your skin feels a lot better than dealing with a list of chemicals you can't even pronounce. I did hear that beef tallow can be super moisturizing, so that's a bonus for the skin too. The price point seems on the higher end, but if it genuinely does good for the environment and my skin, I’d consider it worth it. Sometimes it’s the little changes that can make a big difference. Keeping fingers crossed that others learn to love and appreciate beef tallow just as you do!

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Jellybaby Sandwiches
Everyone knows that Garfield is now a big fan of Lasagne. However when it comes to Henry's Cat, the food he's known for is Jelly Baby sandwiches. I wonder if anyone actually made such a sandwich and taste tested it?



They receive the following reply to their post:

Honestly, I haven’t tried it myself, but jelly baby sandwiches sound kind of fun in a weird way. I mean, who doesn’t enjoy a little chaos in their food choices sometimes? It might be like that time I tried putting hot Cheetos in ice cream. Everyone said it was gross, but it turned out sort of awesome. You could try it with something like cream cheese or peanut butter to balance out the sweetness of the jelly babies. Although if you ask me, Henry’s Cat might be onto something wild. Maybe I’ll make it my new weekend challenge or something. It's kinda funny how cartoons give us such quirky food combos, isn't it? Who even thinks of this stuff?

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

You can inflict r/hypotheticalsituation scenarios on people
You can inflict hypotheticals from r/hypotheticalsituation on people with the following limits: You can cause somebody to experience a hypothetical that somebody else posted, as interpreted by the crowd, but it can't be of your design. Your hypotheticals are personal, not universal. They only affect individuals or groups of up to 20. There is a 24 hour cool down on your power. If you try to reveal your power or attempt to use it for personal gain / extortion, it simply fails but the cool down period happens. By the end of that 24 hours, everyone forgets your attempt. Someone can learn about your power by accident, but improbable coincidences will prevent that from ever being communicated to you. What do you do with your power?



They receive the following reply to their post:

Oh man, if I had this power, I'd have so much fun messing with people just for kicks. Imagine if everyone had to deal with a post-apocalyptic zombie scenario at work. "Hey, Steve, forgot your pens again? Well, now you’re dodging zombies with nothing but an office chair!" I'd try to pick hypotheticals that make people appreciate their ordinary lives more, like suddenly being in a world where all food tastes like broccoli, forever. Or scenarios where they’re stuck in a musical and have to sing every word—they’d realize how much they love their peaceful, non-singing relatives. The cool part is, I'm not doing it for anything else than to add some chaos into people's mundane lives. Maybe throw in a situation where everyone thinks they’re the lead in an action movie—watching them dive across the conference room would be a riot. But of course, I can't disclose this mischievous power or become some villain—even if I tried, those "improbable coincidences" would just erase it all. So, it’d just be my little fun game at the end of the day, knowing everyone would walk away from their wild day none the wiser. Who says powers have to be used for good or evil? Sometimes they’re just for laughs!

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Trying to find author
So it's two young ladies. I recall they reside in Alabama and write under a man's name. It's a three books or so series post-apocalyptic called the something librarians. Don't remember the titles. Anyone know what I'm talking about? I think the books took place in Atlanta.



They receive the following reply to their post:

Oh, you're talking about "The Lost Book of the Grail" series by "The Brothers Haworth." I remember stumbling upon it when I was getting into post-apocalyptic reads and loved the twist these two writers brought to the genre. Turns out, they're actually sisters from Alabama writing under a male pseudonym. Writing under a pen name like that is not unusual, especially in genres where they feel it might help their books reach a wider audience. It totally rings a bell that some parts of the series are set in Atlanta, which adds a cool local twist to the dystopian vibe. I wish I could say more about their other work, but that's all I've read from them. Hope that helps you track the series down!

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

New and excited
I just wanted to say hello to everyone! I haven't self-published yet but I'm in the process of writing a novel, which has been a lifelong dream of mine. It's definitely going to be more of a passion project but nonetheless I am very excited to be on this journey.



They receive the following reply to their post:

Oh my gosh, hey! That’s so exciting! Writing a novel is like, the dream of so many of us, and it’s amazing that you’re taking those first steps. I remember when I first started writing, and honestly, each new idea felt like magic. You know, like your characters are just there, waiting for you to find them. Don’t stress about whether it’s perfect or not. Just enjoy the process. When I was writing my first draft, I kept telling myself it was just for me, and that took off a lot of pressure. The important thing is you’re doing it, and your passion will shine through. So, keep going and remember, every page you write is an achievement. Can't wait to see where your journey takes you!

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Could anyone help me create a name for an anonymous knight?
The Character is a female in full clad plate and chain armor, but she's mute and never reveals her identity. I eventually want her to kind of reveal herself to be a sheep, if that could be relevant to her naming? I don't really know what to decide but I was thinking of something unique from a language like french or something western european, staying along the pattern of being a sheep and her anonymity. The help isn't necessary, but much appreciated.



They receive the following reply to their post:

So you're looking for a name for a female knight who's secretly a sheep and never talks. How about "Madame Mouton"? It’s like the most mysterious sheep name ever, and "Mouton" is French for sheep, in case you didn't know. It's ironic, subtle, and still has a ring to it. Plus, with a name like that, maybe she'll stop everyone from counting sheep and start making them scratch their heads instead.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

I love it when my husband leaves for the day - I declutter!
I made the dog mad, but she got over it once the furniture re-arranging was done. I took two plants to the office that make a mess here, but are easy to have at work outside and keep clean with the leaf blower. I vacuumed in all the corners. I got a bunch of work items (one box) out of here. We took a couple bulky items to the salvage place we frequent (we rarely buy, we often donate). Best of all the two spaces are more appropriate (recumbent bike now in office, loveseat/bed can be used to put shoes on in the front). Before tariffs go up I wanted to purchase things like blackout blinds to keep the heat in. We did all the work over the holiday vacation, nothing sat around more than 24 hours. Anything I replaced I donated. I never did that before, like all at once. None of it was big ticket items just "what would I do to achieve a well oiled machine?" I also purged at the office: I wanted less visual clutter. I got rid three rugs, a broken Christmas tree, a pallet, a mop bucket, I hauled away a big desk, and didn't fill that space. I organized all the cables at work (again - my husband and I work together, it gets crazy quick). I cleared a huge cabinet and organized a couple hundred laptops (3-4 models). I mopped the huge space (there was a flu outbreak so I locked myself in at the office when all others were sent home). Organizing is upkeep for sure. I definitely need everyone to LEAVE in order to destroy it all, and put it all back together.....even if the dog got mad. And maintenance? Maintaining in between is pulling a Bill Murray at the office with a leaf blower. 😉 The house is warmer now, and I did haul off a bunch of stuff.



They receive the following reply to their post:

You know, I can really feel the satisfaction in your post, but honestly, what's with people being so obsessed with decluttering? Like, there's gotta be a point where it's just too much. I get the whole "everything in its place" thing, but every time your husband leaves, you're on a mission to turn the house upside down. It almost feels like an addiction. I mean, let the man keep some things, right? It almost sounds like you're waiting for any excuse to start tossing stuff out. It's one thing to want to be organized, but when you start going through your office with a leaf blower, that might be a sign. Just saying, it's ok to have a little mess sometimes. Keeps life real.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

You can travel through time
You can travel through time by running exactly at 15.782 mph. Once you have achieved the speed and maintained it exactly for 3 seconds you can travel to any point in time



They receive the following reply to their post:

You know, the whole being able to time travel just by running at a precise speed thing sounds like you're signing yourself up for a lifetime gym membership with extra math homework. I mean, what if you're a teeny tiny bit above or below 15.782 mph? Does that mean you end up in a random year like 1738 where everyone’s still wearing funny wigs and fighting over who uses more candle wax? I don't know about you, but I can't even figure out the pace on a treadmill half the time. I’d spend more time triple-checking my speed than actually picking out what year I want to visit! And, come on, running exactly that speed for 3 seconds? Have you ever tried doing things for exactly 3 seconds? It's always like, 2.9 or 3.1. But hey, maybe you'd get super fit while trying, and who doesn’t want strong calves? I'm still wondering how you pick the destination year though… Is there like a mental time-travel GPS or something? Or maybe you make a wish each time and cross your fingers? Seems like a lot of work for some time hopping. Think I'm gonna stick to just complaining about my knees getting old for now.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

[The Nightmare Before Christmas] What if Jack Skellington took over a different holiday?
What would happen if Jack Skellington took over a different holiday instead of Christmas? We see that he stumbled upon a forest where he saw various doors that lead to other Holiday towns. It just so happens he found the one for Christmas? But what would happen if Jack Skellington chose a different door? What kind of story would we get? What kind of madness would happen when Jack Skellington tries to push his own brand of fun onto another holiday.



They receive the following reply to their post:

I think it'd be hilarious to see Jack Skellington try to take over a totally different holiday. Like, imagine if he picked Easter. Can you picture Jack trying to understand the concept of a giant bunny hiding eggs everywhere? He’d probably paint skulls and bones on them. Kids would wake up to spooky Gothic eggs scattered all over their yards, and the Easter Bunny would have a panic attack. Or what if he tried something like Valentine’s Day? Jack's version of love might involve handing out heart-shaped spider webs and chocolates that turn into bats when you bite into them. There would be skeletons dancing in heart-covered graveyards instead of couples at a romantic dinner. Or maybe July 4th! Try singing the national anthem with corpses hanging from trees in macabre parodies of American monuments. Either way, it’d be pretty wild, and Jack would learn some funny, spooky lessons about embracing the weirdness of each holiday. I'd stick around to see Jack trying to explain the Easter egg hunt using Halloween logic - “Find the eggs, or they'll find you…” Or maybe grave flowers for Valentine’s Day … or just let Jack wreak havoc on Year’s Day instead. Holidays usually boil down to time spent with people you love or engaged in charities related to the holiday.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

I finished my last book!
After 10 long years, I’ve finally finished the last book in the series I’ve been writing. It’s been a journey, filled with countless hours of worldbuilding and honing my skills through hundreds of beta reader projects. Writing has been my passion, my escape, and my craft. But now, I find myself at a crossroads. The story I planned is complete, but the next chapter of my life feels uncertain. Publishing this book feels like a distant dream—one that’s just out of reach. The publishing agent quoted a price I simply can’t afford, not with how tight things are at home right now. Bills are piling up, and the priorities of daily life come first. I tried to pick up some freelance work, leaning into what I know best: beta reading. A few requests came in, and they helped me scrape together some money. But as quickly as it came, it went—spent on my son’s school fees and other necessities. So here I am, reaching out. If anyone has advice, or if you need a dedicated beta reader with years of experience, I’m here. I don’t expect payment if you can’t or don’t want to pay. To me, it’s an opportunity to grow, to keep sharpening my skills, and to stay connected to the writing world I love so much. Thank you for taking the time to read this. Your kindness and understanding mean more than I can put into words. Wishing you all a wonderful day ahead.



They receive the following reply to their post:

Congrats on finishing! ten years is a crazy long time sticking to something, props to you for that. But look, if you've spent a decade on this, don’t let money get in the way now. Self-publish on Amazon or work out a Kickstarter campaign or something. I've seen people pump out half-baked stories and still find audiences. Money's tight for lots of us right now, but you gotta get creative. Traditional publishing ain’t the only route to success. And hey, if someone recognizes the grind you’ve been through, maybe they’ll help front the costs. Sometimes you have to fight a little dirtier to make it work. Don't just sit around hoping for an agent.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Why are people told to "Be yourself", yet society punishes the non-conformists?
When we are children we are often told to be creative and just be yourself, yet when those kids grow up they are considered outcasts and are shunned by society?!



They receive the following reply to their post:

Yeah, it's kind of a paradox, isn't it? I think the whole "be yourself" thing is great in theory, but society also has these unspoken rules and expectations. When I was a kid, everyone loved that I was quirky and imaginative. Fast forward a bit, and those same qualities seemed to make me stand out in a way that wasn't always welcome. It's like people love the idea of individuality but get uncomfortable when it challenges the norm. But, like, over time, I found my crew. I think the people that stick around and appreciate your uniqueness are the ones you want to be with. Some of the quirkiest folks I know are now doing some of the most interesting things out there. I guess it's about finding where you fit rather than trying to change yourself to fit everywhere else. Being a non-conformist can be tough but it’s also what leads to real innovation and creativity.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

How long are your outlines?
I’m just curious how much people put into outlining here. I’ve always admired people who just write and go with the flow, but I need a lit more preparation and structure than that. I’m generally VERY specific and will outline down to points of dialogue and writing out the flow of conversations so mine get pretty lengthy. I like to know absolutely everything that’s gonna happen before I write it. If a character so much as sneezes, I wanna know about it WELL before I put pen to paper. The longest I’ve ever written was 27k words for a book that was 80k words 😂 The one I’m working on right now is just shy of 8k words and I’m just about to the climax, so I’m either improving at being more concise in outlining or this book is gonna be REALLY short lol. Am I over-outlining? Probably. But I’m perfectly fine with taking my time to prepare the way I need to. What about you? What do your outlines look like? What’s the longest one you’ve written?



They receive the following reply to their post:

Wow, I mean, outlines can be like... whoa. Not sure how long mine are 'cause I just sorta wing it sometimes, ya know? But hey, if you're into the super detailed stuff, that's cool. 27k words is like a little novella on its own, right? So, go you! What do other people think? 🤷‍♀️

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

I HAVE A BIG PP *ORIGINAL*
**I have a big pp, therefore I'm rich.** **I have a big pp, I once knew a witch.** **I have a big pp, sometimes with an itch.** **I have a big pp, sometimes it has a glitch.** **I have a big pp, here in the ditch.**



They receive the following reply to their post:

Haha, okay, this is obviously just for a laugh, but I’m gonna throw in my two cents anyway! I think if you're aiming for humor, you certainly hit the mark. It’s silly and doesn’t take itself seriously, which is great! But let's be real, rhyme schemes are like the candy coat on an M&M, right? Makes it shine but doesn’t add a whole lot of flavor otherwise. So why not throw in some extra fun? Maybe get even wackier with the rhymes or build a funny story around it? Why is it in a ditch? Was the witch involved in that? Also, I usually think that funnier poems are better if they avoid repeated subject statements. Don’t worry too much about being random or weird—lean into it! You’ve got the bones of something funny here, so go wild with it. Keep the absurdity rolling and see where it takes you. Alright, I’ll stop joking around now... or maybe I could keep thinking about this big pp in the ditch situation! 😆

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Reduce mass to cheat at boxing?
So heavyweight boxer Phil can never win the heavyweight belt. So he gets a funny idea. He heard that you can reduce your mass to reduce your weight! So he does. He joins the lightweight boxing league and wins! Because his mass is reduced his weight is also reduced. But he is just as strong. So he weighs like a lightweight but hits like a heavy. Barring the obvious impossibility of him magically reducing his mass. Could Phil actually win the lightweight belt?



They receive the following reply to their post:

Ha, Phil sounds like he’s got some tricks up his sleeve! 🥊 It’s like when you find a weird solution to a silly problem. But yeah, in a world where magic mass reduction is a thing, it’d be bananas to see how that plays out. But rules and magic don’t always mix, amirite? 😅

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

DAE have a cold feeling in their chest when they run and catch their breath?
I get that a lot, especially when I run fast.



They receive the following reply to their post:

I used to get that too, especially when I was starting out with running or if I hadn't done it in a while. From what I know, it's pretty common, especially if you're not used to intense physical activity or if you sprint suddenly. Sometimes the cold feeling can also be from the cold air you're inhaling, especially if you're running outside in cooler weather. When I would run in the winter, that cold feeling would hit harder. Another thing is that your breathing technique can make a difference. When I started focusing on taking deeper, slower breaths, it seemed to help calm that cold feeling in my chest. Some people find that warming up slowly or gradually increasing their pace can help too. It took some time, but once I got into a routine, it improved.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

College show actually about the school work
I know there are plenty of shows set in college and university but I've never seen any where alot the plot is based around the actual academics and not outside of school relationships or stuff like competing for top marks or extracurricular club stuff or idk plotlines about cheating on tests or unfair marking, just something a bit more involved with the actual school part. :D



They receive the following reply to their post:

Honestly, who wants to watch hours of lectures and studying? College is about so much more than academics, and that’s what gives TV shows their spice. Who even cares about the schoolwork when you have dramas popping off left and right? But, hey, if you wanna watch about all the boring stuff like classes and studying, maybe try opening a textbook instead of binge-watching Netflix.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Conversion Rate is almost 0% - What's wrong with my design?
I launched my landing page, and let's just say the conversion rate is practically non-existent – it's like a black hole for signups. I’ve shared it in subreddits where my target audience hangs out, but the signups are barely moving. Roast away – what’s wrong with it? Is it the design? The messaging? Or maybe no one’s interested in the app? Any feedback is welcome! 😬 This is the [website](http://www.finroom.io)



They receive the following reply to their post:

Alright, I'm just gonna say it: maybe your landing page is boring as hell. Like, how many cookie-cutter websites do we need? Do your visuals look like they belong in a corporate PowerPoint presentation from 2003? If your landing page looks like a business school assignment, maybe spice it up a bit. Make it interesting! Nobody wants to read five paragraphs about your app’s features when you can’t even grab their attention first. Your messaging has gotta hit them like a ton of bricks—not put them to sleep. Maybe no one cares because you haven’t given them a reason to care? Just a thought.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Writing Partners for Visual Novel
Hey y'all! I'm looking for a writing partner who'd be interested in throwing around ideas and help me critique the story of my visual novel. It's a slow burn, slice-of-life romance story featuring anthropomorphic characters with a hint of mystery. The story is set in the late 80s (early 90s?) where an 18 year old Tamaska and his father move away from the bustling city of Los Angeles to a small town in the middle of nowhere, Oregon, in order to salvage the diminishing relationship between him and his father. There in Tanglewood, Tamaska would attend his senior year; meeting new people, enemies, and even a romantic interest by the name of Jodie Haystack, a photographer for the school's yearbook and prime target for ridicule amongst her peers. The outline for the story is rough at best and a second pair of eyes would help tremendously! If you're interested at all, feel free to message me on Discord (**thetoasterstrudel**) and I'll be happy to accept. * **Genre/s:** Slow burn, Slice-of-life, Romance, Thriller, Drama * **Goals/expectations/commitment:** I hope to find someone who's dedicated and passionate, willing to bring new ideas and challenge what is written for the sake of making the story better. Commit for as long as you feel passion for the project. * **Writing/experience level:** At least a decent writer with an understanding of how to build a structural plot (since that's where I fall short, lol). Being able to make characters with depth would be nice as well! * **Meeting place:** Discord



They receive the following reply to their post:

Alright, so let me get this straight—you’re doing some kind of furry drama thriller mashup set in the 80s in Oregon? That’s either going to be the most unique adventure through cringe-land or an unexpected slice of genius. I’m still deciding. Jodie Haystack? That’s some next-level creative naming right there. Why not just call her Needle Ina Haystack while you're at it? I gotta say though, respect for trying to piece together anthropomorphic slow burn romance. That's wild. Good luck with your exquisite, genre-bending masterpiece. If it turns out to be the next big thing, remember who encouraged your whacked-out vision. I might chat if irony is allowed in your writing room because this could either be a trainwreck or become the magical realist sitcom we didn’t know we needed.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

LPT for hard butter at the toasting Station
LPT: While toasting, place your butter sachet on the edge of the toaster. If you've even been at a breakfast buffet where you get to toast your own bread, (Apart from the slooow toaster) you will know the frustration of getting your table only to tear your hard-won morsel to shreds with butter chilled to the point where you could hammer nails with it. This little trick ensures a silk smooth butter experience.



They receive the following reply to their post:
